images.title: Four turns fit a square
images.purpose: Show that a square tile fits its own outline after 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees, the full turn included.
images.composition: One large square with a centre dot on the left, and a single column of four small squares on the right with wide space around all of them.
images.exact_structure: Left: one teal #0072B2 square with a centre dot and a grey #6B7280 curved arrow showing a quarter turn about the dot, a reddish purple #CC79A7 tick on the top left corner. Right: 4 small plain squares in one column, each with the same kind of tick, at the top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left corners in that order. Exactly 1 large square, 4 small squares, 5 ticks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
small squares that are not all the same size
images.takeaway: A square fits its outline after 4 turns, the full turn included.
images.description: A teal square with a centre dot and a quarter turn arrow, beside four small squares showing the corner tick after 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to follow the tick corner by corner and count the turns aloud, ending with the full turn.

image_decisions.why: Counting the four turns, full turn included, is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
